REDSCORE · PRACTICAL PREPAREDNESS

Digital public communication for civil protection and preparedness

Digital public communication can lead to a practical action: checking stock, finding a warning source or recording a contact. This guide is for initiatives, associations and communication teams. It covers editorial basics, not an automatically available government campaign platform.

Updated: 7 November 2026 · RedScore editorial team

On this page

  • Give the content a clear purpose
  • Build a simple editorial plan
  • Make content accessible
  • Identify publishers and sources
  • Handle feedback appropriately
  • Keep measurement proportionate

Give the content a clear purpose

Explain the benefit and the next step. A preparedness post should offer a manageable action as well as attract attention. Educational material before an emergency has a different purpose from a current danger warning. Decide whether you are explaining a subject, encouraging preparation or referring readers to a responsible source.

Build a simple editorial plan

Collect recurring audience questions and prioritise practical value. Your plan could alternate between supplies, lighting, information channels and documents. Link detailed guides rather than placing every detail in every post. Assign responsibility for checking and corrections, and allow time to answer questions.

Make content accessible

Use short headings, readable contrast and descriptive link text. Provide important statements as text, not only within images. Check phone layouts and offer suitable print versions. Translations should preserve meaning and uncertainty. A shareable source link can be more useful than an unattributed image.

Identify publishers and sources

Clearly identify the publisher and link original specialist sources. Label your examples and general scenarios. Avoid presenting third-party logos or official wording in a way that implies a partnership. Show when information was updated and make meaningful corrections visible.

Handle feedback appropriately

Decide how to answer questions and correct mistakes. Refer immediate danger to responsible services rather than treating comments as an emergency channel. Do not request sensitive health, location or identity information in public. Share verified information while respecting affected people's privacy.

Keep measurement proportionate

Separate impressions, clicks and voluntary feedback from completed preparedness. Pageviews alone do not prove better emergency outcomes. Use lawfully collected statistics and respect consent choices. RedScore's public guides and calculators may be linked as independent resources; this does not make them an official system or create a partnership.

Official source

RedScore is an independent service. There is no official partnership. Follow official warnings and instructions in an emergency.
